criteria.description: identity.sanitize_user_id is the chosen mechanism (NOT a separate registry module) and it rejects '_shared' as a user_id, so no minted/resolvable user can alias the shared namespace. '_shared' currently passes the existing charset regex [a-z0-9_-]+, so this is a genuine new check added at the identity boundary. The reservation lives at the identity boundary (sanitize_user_id); the document helpers are NOT expected to independently re-reject '_shared'.
criteria.verifyBy: A pinned test in the identity test module asserts sanitize_user_id('_shared') is rejected per the existing convention (returns None / falsy, matching how other invalid ids are handled), while a plain id like 'matt' still passes through unchanged. Run with .venv/bin/python -m pytest.

criteria.description: A document seeded in documents/_shared/ appears in list_documents(user_id) for two or more distinct users (e.g. 'matt' and 'sarah', plus a third user). list_documents signature is unchanged — still list_documents(user_id).
criteria.verifyBy: Pure-helper test (no TestClient) in tests/test_documents_list_load.py using conftest-monkeypatched docs_dir: seed a doc under _shared/, assert its doc_id is present in list_documents('matt'), list_documents('sarah'), and a third user (using the existing asyncio.run pattern for the async helper).

criteria.description: Each user's own uploads remain invisible to other users after adding the shared union — the existing mirror-image isolation behavior is preserved. A doc under documents/<userA>/ does NOT appear in list_documents(userB).
criteria.verifyBy: Extend mirror-image test in tests/test_documents_list_load.py: seed a per-user doc for 'matt', assert it appears in list_documents('matt') but NOT in list_documents('sarah'); and vice versa. Existing document isolation tests stay green.

criteria.description: list_documents de-duplicates on shadow collision keyed on doc_id: when a user has their own doc with the same doc_id as a shared doc, list_documents(user_id) returns that doc_id EXACTLY ONCE, as the user's version (matching load-resolution), not as a duplicate picker entry.
criteria.verifyBy: Test in tests/test_documents_list_load.py: seed doc_id 'D' with distinct content/title under both documents/<matt>/ and documents/_shared/; assert list_documents('matt') contains exactly one entry whose id == 'D' and whose title/metadata are matt's (not the shared one).

criteria.description: Backward-compat when _shared/ is absent: with no documents/_shared/ directory present, list_documents behavior is unchanged — a fresh user with no uploads gets [], and existing users get only their own docs. The shared union must be keyed strictly on _shared/ presence so it does not regress the empty/absent-_shared path.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: with no _shared/ dir seeded, assert list_documents('dev') == [] for a fresh user and that a user with only their own docs sees exactly those. The existing test_documents_are_user_scoped (which asserts an empty list for a fresh 'dev' user while other users' dirs exist) stays green.

criteria.description: No minted/resolvable user_id can equal '_shared': because sanitize_user_id rejects '_shared' (c1), the union inside list_documents is the ONLY surface through which documents/_shared/ contents reach a user's picker. The document helpers do not independently reject '_shared'; the reservation is enforced solely at the identity boundary, so shared docs surface exclusively via the union for a real minted user.
criteria.verifyBy: Executable test: (a) assert sanitize_user_id('_shared') is rejected (falsy), demonstrating no resolvable identity can be '_shared'; and (b) seed a doc in documents/_shared/ and assert it appears via list_documents('matt') (the union path). Concrete pass/fail; no reviewer judgment.

criteria.description: load_document(user_id, doc_id) resolves the user's own namespace first, then falls back to _shared/ on miss. A shared doc loads successfully for two different users. Signature unchanged: load_document(user_id, doc_id).
criteria.verifyBy: Pure-helper test: seed a doc only in _shared/, assert load_document('matt', shared_id) and load_document('sarah', shared_id) both return non-None content matching the seeded doc.

criteria.description: load_document(user_id, doc_id) still returns None for a doc that belongs to another user and is not in _shared/ (cross-user isolation for load unchanged).
criteria.verifyBy: Test: seed a doc only under documents/<sarah>/, assert load_document('matt', sarahs_doc_id) returns None.

criteria.description: Shadowing is deterministic for load: when a user has their own doc with the same doc_id as a shared doc, load_document(user_id, doc_id) returns the USER's doc, not the shared one.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: seed doc_id 'D' with distinct content under both documents/<matt>/ and documents/_shared/; assert load_document('matt', 'D') returns matt's content, while load_document('sarah', 'D') (no own copy) returns the shared content.

criteria.description: save_upload(user_id, ...) NEVER writes to documents/_shared/ — uploads always land in the acting user's namespace directory, and a pre-existing _shared/ is left byte-for-byte unchanged. This holds both for normal users AND closes the aliasing hole: because sanitize_user_id rejects '_shared' at the identity boundary (c1), save_upload is never reached with user_id='_shared', so the app has no write path into _shared/ at all. Signature unchanged: save_upload(user_id, ...).
criteria.verifyBy: Test: pre-seed documents/_shared/ with a sentinel doc; snapshot the _shared/ directory contents (filenames + bytes); call save_upload for two different users; assert (a) each user's saved file exists under documents/<user_id>/, (b) the _shared/ snapshot is unchanged (same filenames, same bytes, no new entries). Additionally assert that sanitize_user_id('_shared') is falsy (c1) so no request can drive save_upload with '_shared' as the acting user — pinning that the aliasing write-path is closed upstream.

criteria.description: No signature changes to the touched document helpers: list_documents(user_id), load_document(user_id, doc_id), save_upload(user_id, ...) keep their exact existing signatures; and list_documents remains a coroutine. The shared namespace is an internal resolution fallback only.
criteria.verifyBy: inspect.signature checks in a test confirming parameter names/order unchanged from pre-sprint for all three helpers; plus assert asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(list_documents) is True (async-ness preserved); plus all existing call sites remain valid.

criteria.description: The full existing test suite stays green, including the mirror-image isolation suite and the pinned static_prompt_hash literals; bot.py prompt content is untouched.
criteria.verifyBy: Run .venv/bin/python -m pytest (full suite) and confirm all tests pass with no modifications to bot.py prompt content.

scope.description: Code changes limited to documents.py (shared-namespace resolution fallback + list union/dedup) and a single reserved-name guard in identity.sanitize_user_id. No other production modules edited.
No changes to route/endpoint signatures, identity.py cookie logic (beyond the _shared rejection in sanitize_user_id), or bot.py static prompt content.

claims.py shared-sidecar behavior, per-user state modules (sessions/recaps/study history), UI/picker labeling, migration scripts, and copying actual demo documents into _shared/ are out of scope for this sprint (Sprint 0 covers document resolution + list union/dedup + save_upload + the _shared name reservation only).

Tests are pure-helper only (no TestClient), extend the existing mirror-image patterns, and use conftest monkeypatched path constants (docs_dir); no files are deleted; pipecat stays pinned; nothing pushed or merged (run branch only).

criteria.description: Public signatures are EXACTLY unchanged: generate_claims(user_id, doc_id, document_text) and load_fresh_claims(user_id, doc_id, document_text) keep their current 3-parameter signatures with NO additions of any kind (no new positional, keyword-only, or defaulted parameters). All namespace resolution is derived INSIDE the helpers (see c2), never via a caller-supplied parameter, per binding constraint #1 / spec §5.2.
criteria.verifyBy: Test uses inspect.signature to assert the exact ordered parameter lists equal ['user_id','doc_id','document_text'] for both generate_claims and load_fresh_claims — full equality, not merely 'no new required positional'. A positional call (user_id, doc_id, text) also succeeds.

criteria.description: claims.py determines the resolving namespace itself, mirroring documents.load_document, using DOCUMENT presence (the <doc_id>.txt file), NOT sidecar presence, and NOT by importing documents.py. A doc_id resolves to _shared/ IFF DOCUMENTS_DIR/<user_id>/<doc_id>.txt is absent AND DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.txt is present; otherwise it resolves per-user. Because the decision keys on the .txt document (not the sidecar), extraction can bootstrap a _shared/ sidecar that does not yet exist. The document text parameter is named document_text (matching c1).
criteria.verifyBy: Test: seed only DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.txt (no sidecar anywhere) under the monkeypatched claims_docs_dir, call generate_claims(user, doc_id, text); assert the sidecar is created at DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.claims.json (bootstrapped from nothing) and none under the user dir. Separately, static/import test confirms claims.py does not import documents.py (its import closure stays anthropic + stdlib only).

criteria.description: A shared document's claim sidecar path is DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.claims.json; a per-user document's sidecar path is DOCUMENTS_DIR/<user_id>/<doc_id>.claims.json. generate_claims writes to _shared/ IFF the document resolved from _shared/ per c2; otherwise per-user exactly as today.
criteria.verifyBy: Test A: seed only DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.txt under monkeypatched claims_docs_dir, call generate_claims(user, doc_id, text); assert sidecar exists at DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.claims.json and NOT under DOCUMENTS_DIR/<user_id>/. Test B: seed only DOCUMENTS_DIR/<user_id>/<doc_id>.txt, call generate_claims; assert sidecar exists under the user dir and NOT in _shared/.

criteria.description: Generate-once, serve-everyone: after a shared sidecar is extracted a single time, load_fresh_claims returns those same claims for MULTIPLE different users (at least three: A who generated, plus B and C with no prior state) on the same shared doc id, with NO re-extraction, and with no per-user sidecar ever written.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: seed DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.txt; with extract_claims patched to a mock, call generate_claims as user A once, then load_fresh_claims for users A, B, and C with the same doc_id+text. Assert all three return the identical claims payload; assert the extract_claims mock was called EXACTLY once across all four calls (mock.call_count == 1); assert exactly one sidecar file exists (in _shared/) and none exist under any user's dir.

criteria.description: load_fresh_claims resolves user-first then _shared/, keyed on document presence per c2: a user who owns their own <doc_id>.txt (with its per-user sidecar) shadows a colliding _shared/ doc+sidecar, deterministically.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: under monkeypatched claims_docs_dir seed BOTH DOCUMENTS_DIR/<user>/<doc_id>.txt (with a per-user sidecar of distinguishable claim content) AND DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.txt (with a distinguishable shared sidecar), same doc_id; assert load_fresh_claims(user, doc_id, text) returns the USER's claims, not the shared ones.

criteria.description: A per-user document's sidecar stays strictly per-user (mirror-image isolation for claims): no fallback from one user to another. A doc that exists only in user A's namespace yields A a per-user sidecar; user B (who has no such doc and no shared doc) gets a miss, never A's claims.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: seed only DOCUMENTS_DIR/<A>/<doc_id>.txt, generate claims as A; then call load_fresh_claims(B, doc_id, text) where B has neither a user doc nor a shared doc for doc_id; assert B gets a miss (None / regenerate, never A's cached claims) and that no sidecar exists under B's dir or in _shared/.

criteria.description: source_hash freshness is unchanged and is evaluated ONLY in the namespace the DOCUMENT resolves to (per c2). A stale sidecar (source_hash mismatch vs current text) in the resolved namespace is a miss exactly as today; a matching source_hash is served without regeneration. Cross-namespace fall-through is forbidden: when the document resolves per-user, the _shared/ sidecar is never consulted (a stale user sidecar is a miss and does NOT silently return fresh shared claims); when the document resolves from _shared/, the per-user sidecar is never consulted.
criteria.verifyBy: Tests on a _shared/-resolved doc (only DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.txt seeded): (a) matching text -> load_fresh_claims returns the cached shared claims without rewriting the sidecar; (b) changed text -> does not return stale claims (miss/regenerate). Collision test: seed DOCUMENTS_DIR/<user>/<doc_id>.txt (doc resolves per-user) with a STALE per-user sidecar AND a FRESH _shared/ sidecar of the same doc_id; assert load_fresh_claims(user, doc_id, text) treats the stale per-user sidecar as a miss and does NOT return the fresh shared claims (no cross-namespace fall-through).

criteria.description: The shared-vs-per-user namespace PLACEMENT decision is centralized in a single path: generate_claims is the only function that DECIDES which namespace a sidecar is written into (i.e. the only function that computes the _shared/-vs-user resolution before writing). The low-level primitives write_claims (and any _claims_path/path-building helper) remain intact PUBLIC primitives that write to / build a path they are GIVEN and must NOT themselves choose the namespace — they are unchanged so the existing suite that calls write_claims directly stays green. No second function that both resolves the namespace and writes a sidecar exists, so the c3 placement rule governs every caller (including the warm endpoint's background task in app.py, which reaches extraction through generate_claims).
criteria.verifyBy: AST/static test over claims.py: (1) assert write_claims still exists and is callable (existing tests call it directly). (2) Identify the namespace-resolution/placement helper introduced for c2 (the function computing user-first-then-_shared placement for a sidecar target); assert it is invoked only from within generate_claims (not from write_claims or load_fresh_claims's write paths — load_fresh_claims never writes). Equivalently: assert generate_claims is the sole function whose body BOTH performs the _shared-vs-user resolution AND writes a sidecar. app.py is out of scope and not inspected.

criteria.description: Read-only shared happy path: with DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.txt and a fresh DOCUMENTS_DIR/_shared/<doc_id>.claims.json already present and a user who has no per-user doc or sidecar, load_fresh_claims(user, doc_id, text) returns the shared claims (non-None) without invoking extraction.
criteria.verifyBy: Test: pre-seed both the shared .txt and a matching-source_hash shared sidecar; with extract_claims patched to a mock, call load_fresh_claims(user, doc_id, text) for a user with no prior state; assert it returns the shared claims (non-None) and the extract_claims mock was NOT called.

criteria.description: All existing claims tests remain green, and new tests extend the existing mirror pattern in tests/test_claims.py using the monkeypatched claims_docs_dir fixture (no TestClient; pure helpers driven directly; extraction mocked/patched for determinism as in the existing suite). This is the primary deterministic gate for the sprint (the claims verifier runs tests/test_claims.py).

criteria.description: No out-of-scope module is edited, so the broader suite's guarantees (mirror-image isolation and the pinned static_prompt_hash literals) are preserved by construction: this sprint touches only claims.py and tests/test_claims.py, leaving bot.py, documents.py, identity.py, and app.py unmodified. Verified as a human/merge-review + optional-full-run check rather than by the claims-only deterministic verifier.

scope.description: Code changes belong in claims.py (shared-sidecar namespace resolution/placement fallback) plus new/extended tests in tests/test_claims.py. documents.py, identity.py, bot.py, app.py, and route signatures are out of scope for this sprint.

No public signature changes to any helper; _shared support is an internal resolution fallback derived inside the helpers only, per identity spec §5.2. No new parameters of any kind (positional, keyword-only, or defaulted).
claims.py must NOT import documents.py; it preserves its anthropic + stdlib-only import closure and derives the resolving namespace by checking <doc_id>.txt presence directly against DOCUMENTS_DIR.

No UI, no migration, no demo-doc content selection, and no app write path that creates _shared/ DOCUMENTS; writing a shared claim SIDECAR into _shared/ (via generate_claims when the doc resolved from _shared/) is the only permitted _shared/ write. Shared docs/sidecars used by tests are seeded on the filesystem by the tests.
source_hash freshness semantics must not be redefined — only reused for the shared sidecar location, evaluated solely in the namespace the document resolves to, with no cross-namespace fall-through.

Low-level primitives write_claims and any path-building helper stay intact and public (existing tests call write_claims directly); the sprint only adds the namespace-placement decision inside generate_claims. The warm endpoint's background task lives in app.py (out of scope) and inherits correct placement by funneling through generate_claims.

criteria.description: A new test in tests/test_study_history.py seeds DISTINCT study sessions/recaps for two users A and B against the SAME shared document id D (a genuine collision on the isolation key), using conftest's study_history_tmp monkeypatch. It asserts previous_session_recap(A, D, ...) returns content derived only from A's session (e.g., A's covered bullet/marker present) and NOT B's marker, and previous_session_recap(B, D, ...) returns only B's content and NOT A's — cross-exclusion in both directions, not merely non-None.
criteria.verifyBy: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_study_history.py -q passes; the new test asserts distinguishable per-user recap text and that each user's result excludes the other user's marker on the same shared doc id D.

criteria.description: A test asserts that a user C who has NO sessions on shared doc id D receives exactly None from previous_session_recap(C, D, ...), even though users A and B both have sessions on that same D.
criteria.verifyBy: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_study_history.py -q passes; the empty-case assertion is `previous_session_recap(C, D, ...) is None` and is green.

criteria.verifyBy: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_sessions_listing.py -q passes; assertions check membership of the acting user's session record and exclusion of the other user's record for shared doc id D, using the cost_log_tmp fixture (no study_history_tmp misuse).

This exercises the artifacts/transcripts/memory dimension the sprint explicitly names, via the path-isolation mechanism (per-user dirs) that previous_session_recap and session_state already rely on.
criteria.verifyBy: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_study_history.py tests/test_session_state.py -q passes; the new assertions show A's and B's artifacts/transcripts/memory for the same shared doc id D are read back per-user with cross-exclusion, using session_state_tmp and/or the ARTIFACTS_DIR path under study_history_tmp.

criteria.description: The new tests use an identical shared document_id constant for both users A and B (proving the isolation key is user_id + document_id, not a differing doc id), rely solely on the appropriate module-path monkeypatch fixtures (study_history_tmp for recap tests, cost_log_tmp for list_study_sessions tests, session_state_tmp for transcript/memory tests), and add no TestClient / HTTP-level dependency.
criteria.verifyBy: Reading the new tests: both users are exercised with one shared doc_id constant; recap tests use study_history_tmp, listing tests use cost_log_tmp, transcript/memory tests use session_state_tmp; no TestClient import is added.
